This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
The Labor Department showed inflation picking up steam last month. NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose about 12 points in early trading.
Investors think the somewhat hotter-than-expected cost-of-living report makes it more likely the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates when policymakers meet later this month.
Consumer prices in September were up 3.7 percent from a year ago. That's a sharper annual increase than the previous month.
The U.S. war with Iran has triggered a big run-up in energy prices. Rents and restaurant prices are climbing as well.
Average wages are not keeping pace with the higher cost of living. People who depend on social security, however, will get a cost-of-living adjustment of 3.6 percent, beginning in the new year.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
A federal judge has ruled that the Trump administration cannot bar news outlets from the White House that have angered the president, at least for the foreseeable future.
As NPR's David Falkenflick reports, the president announced last month that he was banning journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico because he thought their reporting was too negative.
U.S. District Court Judge Timothy Kelly pointed to a series of statements by Trump attacking the outlets and their reporting.
He wrote that, quote, "It was not hard to conclude. The White House had violated constitutional protections of freedom of speech by retaliating against the three outlets."
And Judge Kelly found violations of due process, too. That is, the administration didn't give CNN, MS Now and Politico any warning or chance to appeal in advance.
The judge wrote that national security concerns are legitimate, but that the administration only cited those after the fact.
The judge's opinion stands until the case goes to trial, but it reveals how he is likely to decide. David Falkenflick, NPR News.
Immigration officials are acknowledging they used a warehouse in Roxbury, New Jersey, for operations.
Court orders forbid converting the site into a detention center. NPR's Jasmine Garst has more.
Earlier this year, Homeland Security purchased 11 warehouses to turn into detention centers.
Several lawsuits by state attorneys general followed, and many of the warehouses are now being sold.
Three of those, which the government still owns, have court orders barring conversion pending environmental assessments.
In recent weeks, NPR received several tips from people who believed loved ones were held at the Roxbury warehouse.
NPR was able to speak to a young man who said he was held in the warehouse parking lot.
In a statement from ICE forwarded to NPR by the Office of New Jersey Representative Annelilia Mejia, officials confirmed they used the parking lot on two occasions.
They say they did not bring anyone detained into the facility. Jasmine Garst, NPR News, New York.
On Wall Street, the Dow is now up more than 40 points. You're listening to NPR.
The man convicted of orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur in 1996 has been sentenced to prison.
Dwayne Davis' sentence is 40 years to life. Shakur's murder was unsolved for years until Davis wrote in a book about it.
He also gave interviews about his role in the shooting death.
In the face of shrinking health budgets, the World Health Organization is updating guidance to make limited vaccine stocks cover more people.
NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports.
Many global vaccination campaigns are funded through foreign aid. As the U.S. and many other countries drastically reduce such spending, many countries are facing tighter vaccine budgets.
On Tuesday, the WHO's Vaccine Advisory Committee recommended smaller dosing regimens for several vaccines.
They recommended that yellow fever vaccine campaigns use one-fifth the typical dose for a single vaccine when there are supply or budgetary constraints to help get the shots into more arms.
And the committee said that the HPV vaccine campaign should use a single dose instead of a two- or three-dose schedule.
The committee stressed that evidence suggests these smaller regimens are still effective and could ultimately help more people get vaccinated.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
Authorities in France say cyber attackers have targeted hundreds of supermarkets. Saboteurs made refrigeration systems in the supermarkets overheat that spoiled food and ignited some fires.
That in turn prompted a leading grocery store to shut down its website, serving customers in the Europe and the U.S.
You're listening to NPR.

topics.text: Labor Department reports September inflation rising to 3.7 percent, Dow rises modestly
Trump administration barred CNN, MS Now and Politico from White House; judge rules against it
Immigration officials acknowledge using Roxbury, New Jersey warehouse parking lot for operations
Dwayne Davis sentenced to 40 years to life for orchestrating 1996 Tupac Shakur murder
WHO updates vaccine guidance recommending smaller doses to stretch limited vaccine supplies
French authorities report cyberattacks overheating refrigeration at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires
